item.title: Docs as Code with AsciiDoc
item.description:
Writing Documentation as Code with AsciiDoc

What is AsciiDoc?

AsciiDoc is a lightweight markup language that allows you to write documentation in plain text. It is designed to be human-readable and supports features like section headers, formatting, tables, links, images, callouts, and much more. AsciiDoc documents can be converted to various output formats such as HTML, PDF, DocBook, and EPUB using tools like Asciidoctor or Pandoc. AsciiDoc can also be included in toolchains like the Maven build tool.

item.title: Taking Notes & Writing Documentation with Markdown
item.description:
Documentation and Note-Taking with Markdown: A Practical Guide

Markdown has become the de facto standard for lightweight text formatting, especially in tech-focused environments. This guide provides an overview of Markdown, its variants, how it compares to AsciiDoc, tools and services that support it, and best practices for writing clean, extensible Markdown documents.
